title: fleet-guards: predictable /tmp state dir without ownership check (suppression vector)
description: 3x codereview of lh2z fix (security finding 1, P3): scripts/fleet-guards.sh:13-14 mkdir -p succeeds silently on a pre-existing /tmp/fleet-driver-state; another local user winning the creation race owns the dir and can suppress the waste alarm (delete snapshot each window) or plant crafted values. Subordinate: fleet_burn.py:37 open(tmp,'w') follows a pre-planted symlink for the PID-named tmp file (arbitrary-file-overwrite race); final os.replace is safe. Prerequisite is a second local account — none today, hence P3. Fix: refuse to run unless [ -O "$STATE" ], or move state under a mode-0700 home path.
